title: Graphic primitive afb.gp.v2
description: The AFB graphic-primitive entity (the only one; afb.gp.v1 was removed). Notable points: (1) the instrument is identified by the full composite `instrument_key` (afbws/common.v1.json#/$defs/instrumentKey) instead of the short `ticker`; (2) new kinds `trendline` and `fibonacci` — both two-anchor primitives; their rendering is not specified yet; (3) the primitive's own parameters (`start`, `stop`, `text`) live in the `settings` dictionary, not at the root, so a kind can gain parameters without touching the envelope. ROOT = identity and server-side ownership: `schema`, `id`, `instrument_key`, `kind`, `tradeplan_id` (all other parameters go to `settings`). `settings` is REQUIRED and strictly typed by `kind` (enforced by the `allOf` below, each branch is additionalProperties:false): line/line_enter/line_sl/line_tp → `primitiveSettingsLine` {start}; note → `primitiveSettingsNote` {start, text? (≤160)}; zone/ruler/trendline/fibonacci → `primitiveSettingsTwoPoint` {start, stop}. The former v1 (`afb.gp.v1`, flat start/stop/text) has been removed. Promotes the parked settings.primitives[secid][] draft (draft/primitive.v1.json) into a strict canonical entity. Whether a primitive is REFERENCED BY a tradeplan's condition is still derived fresh from the tradeplans themselves on every read, never persisted here. OWNERSHIP is different and is persisted — see `tradeplan_id`.

settings.description: Primitive parameters, strictly typed by `kind` (see root description). Replaced as a whole on `set`.

tradeplan_id.description: Владеющий торговый план. Проставляется сервером при компиляции плана в сделку (публикация/amend); снимается только при физическом удалении плана. Клиент это поле не задаёт и не меняет — в set-запросе оно игнорируется в пользу хранимого значения. Пустое/отсутствующее — свободный примитив, доступный любому плану. При архивации плана его уровни физически удаляются из этого хранилища, но условия плана НЕ переписываются в числа — план сохраняет исходные ссылки на примитивы; полная копия каждого удалённого уровня (kind/координаты/стиль) переносится в archived_components плана и является источником его исторической отрисовки.

styleColor.title: Colour of a chart object.
styleColor.description: The only colour format of the style model: `#rrggbbaa`, lowercase hex, the alpha byte is mandatory (`ff` = opaque). Producers normalise `#rrggbb` to `#rrggbbff` and `rgba(r,g,b,a)` to hex with alpha `round(a*255)`.

styleLineWidth.title: Line width.
styleLineWidth.description: Line thickness in pixels, the lightweight-charts `LineWidth` (1..4).

styleLineStyle.title: Line dash style.
styleLineStyle.description: lightweight-charts `LineStyle`: 0 Solid, 1 Dotted, 2 Dashed, 3 LargeDashed, 4 SparseDotted.

styleSeriesType.title: Kind of a line-like series.
styleSeriesType.description: How a non-candle series (dataset field or indicator) is drawn.

lineObjectStyle.title: Display style of a line-like object (primitive kind).
lineObjectStyle.description: Complete style: all keys are required, unknown keys are rejected. Stored per primitive kind (personal row, otherwise the shared one) and read by the primitives plugin, plan levels (`line_enter`/`line_sl`/`line_tp`) and axis labels. For `note` the colour is that of the callout line, frame and text.

seriesStyle.title: Display style of a line-like series (dataset field or indicator).
seriesStyle.description: Complete style: all keys except the optional `bottomColor` are required, unknown keys are rejected. Used for every dataset that is not `candles`, and for chart indicators. `lineWidth`/`lineStyle` are meaningful for Line/Area/Baseline.

bottomColor.description: Colour below the base (0; 50 for `percent`); read only when `seriesType` is `Baseline`; absent means the frontend draws `#ef5350ff`.

candleStyle.title: Display style of the candle series.
candleStyle.description: Complete style: all keys are required, unknown keys are rejected. The wick is drawn in the body colour. Volume bars under the candles use their own up/down colours.

chartType.description: Which series class draws the price: Japanese candles or OHLC bars.

upColor.description: Colour of a rising candle/bar (and its wick).

downColor.description: Colour of a falling candle/bar (and its wick).

volumeUpColor.description: Colour of the volume bar of a rising candle.

volumeDownColor.description: Colour of the volume bar of a falling candle.

datasetStyle.title: Complete display style of a dataset.
datasetStyle.description: `candleStyle` for the `candles` dataset, `seriesStyle` for every other one. The schema only requires one of the two shapes; that the shape fits the dataset's field is checked by the server (`validation_error`). Used in `$defs/dataset.style`.

indicatorSettings.description: Calculation parameters of an indicator (not its look: colour, width and dash style are in `indicator.style`). Typed optional keys of the built-in indicators: period (wma, cot); erPeriod/fastPeriod/slowPeriod (kama); start/maximum/increment (psar). Any other key is allowed (value: number, string or boolean), except `enabled` (per-device view flag, never protocol) and `color`/`lineWidth`/`lineStyle` (moved to `style`) — indicators are computed by the frontend, so a new indicator brings its own parameters without a protocol change. Mirrors the parameter part of IndicatorInstance.settings of the frontend chart.

indicator.title: Chart indicator (user or shared)
indicator.description: `scope: shared` indicators are common to all users and editable only by a manager; `personal` belong to the caller. `settings` carry the calculation parameters only, `style` the complete look of the series. Whether an indicator is shown on the chart is not part of the protocol (per-device view setting kept in the client's localStorage). `type` is an open string (pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`), not an enum; the server computes only wma/kama/psar (alarm indicator conditions, virtual account), other types are stored and returned as is. Type `cot` is chart-only.

type.description: Indicator type, an open set: indicators are computed by the frontend, so a new indicator needs no protocol change. Known: wma, kama, psar, cot.

datasetRef.title: Reference to a primary-data field of a dataset.
datasetRef.description: Grammar: `candles` (the candle series OHLC pseudo-field; price unit, pane `price` only, at most one per preset) | `<source>.<field>` | `<source>.<field>@median(N)` | `<source>.<field>@window(N)`. `@median(N)` is the rolling median of the field in calendar days (same meaning as in afbws/market.channel.v2.json#/$defs/fieldRequest); `@window(N)` is a window of N bars of the chart period, allowed only for fields flagged `window` in `fields.v2` and mandatory for them, N in 2..`window_max_bars` (e.g. `positions.willco@window(180)`). The pattern checks the shape only; the real bounds of N and the existence of the field are enforced by the server registry.

dataset.title: Dataset of a chart (user-visible primary-data series)
dataset.description: A primary-data field (or the candle series) that staff made available, with a name and a style. `scope: shared` is the common series: visible to everyone by `name`, changed and deleted by staff only; a shared preset may reference shared datasets only. `scope: personal` has two meanings told apart by whether a shared dataset with the same `id` exists. With it, the row is the caller's personal style of that series (a "shadow"): only `style` is meaningful, readers take `name`/`field`/`unit` from the shared series and the server copies them from it; any user may create it, it is visible and pushed to its owner only. Without a shared series, it is a staff member's own series, visible to its author only; publishing it means the same row becomes `shared`. `unit` is filled by the server from the field registry and is ignored in `set`. `style` is the complete style (see `$defs/datasetStyle`); the kind-vs-keys check is done by the server.

unit.description: Unit of the field's values, set by the server from the registry; ignored in `set`.

datasetRejection.title: One dataset that was not applied by dataset.set/dataset.delete.

preset.title: Chart preset (user or shared)
preset.description: A snapshot of a chart layout: which datasets are drawn on which pane. `scope: shared` presets are common to all users and editable only by staff; `personal` belong to the caller. `panes` has three panes: `price` (the candle pane), `upper` and `lower` (the two extra panes); each is an array of at most 16 `presetItem`s, the ORDER is the draw and legend order. Rules (checked by the server in `preset.set`, `validation_error` otherwise; the frontend checks them too): at most 16 items per pane; a dataset does not repeat on one pane (it may on different panes); a referenced dataset must exist and be visible to the author; a shared preset may reference shared datasets only. The candle series is not placed in panes. Applying a preset copies its `panes` into the chart slot; later edits of the slot do not change the preset, and later edits of a shared preset do not reach those who applied it. WMA/KAMA/PSAR indicators are not part of a preset.

presetItem.title: One dataset placed on a pane of a preset.
presetItem.description: `dataset` is the id of a dataset (`$defs/dataset.id`). The item carries layout only, no style: the style belongs to the dataset (shared, or the user's personal shadow).

visible.description: Whether the series is shown; a hidden series stays in the layout. Absent means true.

scale.description: Price scale of the series on its pane: `right` = the pane's common right scale, `left` = the pane's common left scale, `own` = the series' own invisible overlay scale (stretched over the pane height). Absent means the default by the dataset's scale class: normalized series (fixed range) on `left`, others on `right`, on the price pane on `own`.

primitiveStyles.title: Per-user display styles of primitives by kind (afbws.gp.style.v2).
primitiveStyles.description: Keys are primitive kinds; a kind that is absent has no stored override (the client falls back to its defaults).
